newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Foreign officials walk out of Mostar ceremony.
newsitem.headline: Foreign officials walk out of Mostar ceremony.

text.p: Foreign officials walked out of a ceremony in the Croat part of Bosnia on Saturday because a Croat official made derogatory remarks about the European Union (EU) and its former administrator in Mostar, western officials said.
Sir Martin Garrod, an international representative in the divided town of Mostar, led the departure in front of Croatian President Franjo Tudjman.
The incident occurred at the opening of an aluminium factory near Mostar.
Eyewitnesses said that Croat official criticised the European Union and its former chief in Mostar Hans Koschnick for not supporting the aluminium factory financially.
He also made reference to a missile attack which Koschnick survived in his Mostar hotel room in 1995.
"He said something in the line that Koschnik deserved what he got," a western official who attended the ceremony said.
Other western officials followed Garrod's example. The Mostar representative of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) Ed Joseph said: "I felt compelled to show solidarity."
